**In one line**: The Trump administration's opposition to AI regulation is at odds with parts of the industry that have urged slowing down and adopting safety rules, according to CNBC.

### Key points
- CNBC reports the Trump administration has maintained its opposition to imposing regulation on the AI industry.
- Meanwhile, some within the industry are said to have pushed for slowing the pace of development, or at least establishing minimal rules, in the name of safety.
- The government's deregulatory stance could weaken the case for such voluntary slowdowns, observers suggest.

### Why it matters
Regulatory direction shapes how fast AI companies build, how much they invest in safety, and the terms on which they enter the market. When the government pushes back on rules, calls to "go slower" tend to lose traction under competitive pressure — a signal of which way the US debate between safety and speed is tilting.
